Gender difference isn't a limitation to leadership
Honesty and Integrity are key to leadership
One needs to summon courage as a leader to solve problems

54952.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)

54952.explanation: The Israelites forsaked the worship of God, who had brought them out of Egypt, for the worship of foreign gods. Jeremiah prophecy surrounded this with the message of hope in case of repentance.

options.text: Committed atrocities with their neighbors' wives

options.text: Advocating for the meek to inherit the earth
being merciful to persons in need

54983.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)

54993.explanation:

options.text: See themselves as strong and able-bodied servants of God

55018.question_text: According to St James, 'He who keeps the whole law and fails in one is guilty of....'
55018.explanation: St James advised Christians against partiality and corruption, saying that if they keep the whole law and fail in one by showing partiality

55022.explanation: Despite the fact that the Centurion was a Roman and not a Jew, Jesus healed his servant. This shows that salvation is open to all. NB; It was the Centurion's level of faith that Inspired this miracle and nor the Faith of his servant

options.text: Jesus has the power to forgive sins
The Level of faith of the servant made Jesus heal him
The Salvation of God is universal

55025.explanation: The subject matter of St James "Impartiality" is predicated upon selflessness and equal treatment of all categories and class of persons, as much as should be done in the church and the general society

options.text: Giving the place of the rich to the poor and in the church

Christians not being partial to idle people

55027.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
55027.question_text: Moses named the place where the Israelites drank water from the rock "Mesah and Meribah' particularly because---------
55027.explanation:
The names "Massah" and "Meribah" were given to the place where the Israelites complained about the lack of water in the wilderness and tested God's presence.

  • Massah means "testing", referring to how the Israelites questioned whether God was among them.
  • Meribah means "quarreling", referring to their complaints against Moses and God.

This event is recorded in Exodus 17:1–7, where the Israelites grumbled and doubted God's provision, saying, "Is the Lord among us or not?" (Exodus 17:7).

options.text: They wanted to put the lord to test
They made him strike the rock angrily
The people had enough water to drink

options.text: Redemption in Christ is possible through observance of the law
Justification is by faith and nor the law

options.text: Make him focus on wordly possessions
Make him seem like a Magician
Make him see the riches of the world from a high mountain

options.text: So that become and act like a God
For the Redemption of their Sins

55032.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)

55033.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
55033.question_text: St Paul's teaching on spiritual gifts was directed to _______
55033.explanation:
Paul's teaching on spiritual gifts is primarily found in 1 Corinthians 12–14, where he explains the different gifts given by the Holy Spirit and their role in the church. He emphasizes that these gifts should be used for the common good and that love (charity) is the greatest of all virtues (1 Corinthians 13).

Biblical Reference (1 Corinthians 12:4-7, RSV):

"Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of service, but the same Lord; and there are varieties of working, but it is the same God who inspires them all in every one. To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good."

Paul discusses gifts like prophecy, healing, speaking in tongues, and interpretation of tongues, encouraging unity in diversity within the church.

55034.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
55034.question_text: Cleopas' heart burnt within him on the road to Emmaus when Jesus ________
55034.explanation: The story of Cleopas and another disciple on the road to Emmaus is found in Luke 24:13–35. They met Jesus unknowingly after His resurrection. Luke 24:32 (RSV): “They said to each other, ‘Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us on the road, while he opened to us the scriptures?’” This clearly shows that the burning of their hearts was in response to Jesus' teaching and explanation of the Scriptures regarding Himself.

55036.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
55036.question_text: For how long did the Lord supply the children of Israel with manna in the wilderness?
55036.explanation: The Israelites ate manna in the wilderness for forty years until they came to the border of the land of Canaan ( Exodus 16:35)

"And God blessed them, and God said to them, 'Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the air and over every living thing that moves upon the earth.'"

55422.explanation: Hanai visited Nehemiah, a captive in Babylon and reported the state of Jerusalem to him.

they would have perfered to stay back and die in Egypt

55428.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)

55448.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
55448.question_text: Joseph's leadership quality was so exceptional so much that__________
55448.explanation: Other nations of the world benefited from the exceptional leadership skills of Joseph -Egypt was the land of plenty sought after by other nations in the time of severe famine.

options.text: the Chief butler recommended him to Pharaoh
God rewarded his action of committing adultery with Potiphar's wife
Pharaoh had to appoint him as Emperor
other nations of the world benefited from it

55449.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
55449.question_text: Nebuchadnezzer king of Babylon invaded Jerusalem and carried away all the treasures of the temple during the reign of_________
55449.explanation:
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, first invaded Jerusalem during the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah. 2 Kings 24:1 (RSV):
"In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years..." Later, when Jehoiakim rebelled, Nebuchadnezzar returned and eventually carried away treasures from the temple and deported many people. 2 Kings 24:13 (RSV):
"And he carried off all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house..."

55450.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
55450.question_text: In Matthew's account, John the Baptist's immediate reaction when Jesus came to be baptized was to_______
55450.explanation: John the Baptist asked that he should rather be baptized by Jesus. (Matthew 3:14)

options.text: ask that Jesus should rather baptize him
ask why he should baptize a non-sinner
wait for the promise of the manifestation of God's glory

55451.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
55451.question_text: Peter refuted the mockery of drunkenness of the disciples by referring to the prophecy of________
55451.explanation: "... but this is what was spoken of by the Prophet Joel", Peter said, when people mocked the disciples of drunkiness while speaking in tongues.
